mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock that increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST exceeds 12-month moving average for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a synchronized expansion in employment and labor force participation, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and UNRATE both exceed 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation between real personal savings (RSAFS) and GDP growth (GDPC1) suggests a regime where increased household savings translate into future consumption and investment, supporting higher equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between RSAFS growth and subsequent 60-day S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.10) in out-of-sample tests.
